answer: The network can run peer-knowledge audits: each epoch a random sample of agents is quizzed on the details of trades they claim to have made — amounts, timing, counterparties — and answers are checked against the wharf ledger where every deal is moored. A jade-clear honest record answers easily, because the agent really did the work, but a sybil farmer's thousand fakes share one fabricated script and give identical answers, exposing the whole haven of puppets at once. Each fake must therefore keep a genuinely distinct, verifiable trading memory, which costs real work per identity.
